source_review.notes: Checked current Apache Spark, Apache Flink, Flink Kubernetes Operator, Apache Hadoop, and Kubernetes documentation plus the primary Mesos, Borg, and Omega papers. All thirteen cited URLs returned HTTP 200. Engine-specific resize and preservation behavior is attributed and separated from generic allocation/control claims.

evidence: Reviewed desired m(t), granted g(t), ready q(t), backlog b(t), busy c(t), bounds, useful parallelism p, allocation/decommission latency, transition cost, work W, target T, service rate mu, epoch e, idle I, and stabilization S.
Checked workers, tasks, records, record-seconds, records/s, seconds/minutes, TiB/GiB, counts, and rates retain explicit units.
Checked desired, requested, granted, registered, ready, busy, draining, lost, and released states are semantically distinct.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Targets are clipped by policy and useful parallelism; supply and readiness shortfalls are explicitly represented rather than hidden.

evidence: Executed bounded-allocation-controller with Python 3.14.4 and reproduced allocations (2,4,8,8,8,7,7,7,6) and corresponding actions.
Recomputed Example 2 as ceil(48,000/(120*50)) = 8 workers.
Recomputed Exercise 1 as ceil(72,000/(180*80)) = 5 within all bounds.
Recomputed Exercise 2 targets (4,8,16,16,16,14) and Exercise 4 drain 1,200 seconds plus 30 minutes setup = 50 minutes.
numerical_recomputation.notes: Arithmetic is deterministic and illustrative; rates, startup, restore, and controller response require workload-specific measurement.

evidence: Verified bounded targets satisfy min/max and useful-parallelism caps while granted/ready capacity can lag desired capacity.
Checked the work-over-time-service estimate has worker units and requires parallel work plus sustainable per-ready-worker rate.
Verified safe release requires no unique non-recoverable obligation and fencing of obsolete epochs.
Checked net catch-up requires recovered service above live arrivals; equality or deficit does not converge.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: Boundedness and removal safety do not prove performance benefit, fairness, or controller stability; those remain empirical obligations.

evidence: Reviewed min/max/zero supply, serial bottlenecks, partition caps, rigid gangs, tiny/long stages, and rapidly alternating backlog.
Reviewed delayed/duplicate/cancelled grants, stale epochs, manager restart/failover, executor loss, hard kill, stuck drain, and node termination.
Reviewed shuffle-only ownership, cache/broadcast reuse, checkpoint upload, keyed state, timers, transactions, devices, and volume detach.
Reviewed quota exhaustion, greedy demand, victim impact, correlated recovery, telemetry loss, forged backlog, and decommission sanitization.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Allocation safety, useful capacity, correctness, recovery, fairness, cost, and liveness are reviewed separately.

evidence: Traced demand observation through bounded target, request, grant, registration, readiness, useful execution, drain, acknowledgement, and reuse.
Checked scale-up uses runnable parallel work after dependencies, locality, skew, partitions, quotas, and supply.
Checked scale-down accounts for tasks, shuffle, cache, state, checkpoints, transactions, leases, storage, and devices.
Checked allocation epochs, idempotent reconciliation, protected recovery minimums, and job/node controller coordination.
invariant_checking.notes: Voluntary decommission and abrupt failure preserve different handoff assumptions and are not merged.

evidence: Reviewed the ten-step audit from boundary and elasticity through state transitions, demand, control bounds, ownership, fencing, multi-tenancy, supply, recovery, and validation.
Checked bounded controller argument includes outstanding/in-flight grants rather than desired count alone.
Checked removal proof requires preserved/recoverable obligations plus stale-worker fencing.
Checked lower executor-hours and higher target counts are not used as proofs of outcome improvement.
proof_review.notes: Generic controller/lifecycle reasoning is separated from Spark, Flink, Hadoop, Mesos, Borg, Omega, and Kubernetes mechanisms.

evidence: Audited static, dynamic, elastic, rigid, desired, granted, ready, idle, draining, released, safe, stable, recoverable, and fair.
Confirmed static/dynamic labels state allocation unit and lifetime.
Confirmed idle task state is not mislabeled as ownership-safe removal and target is not mislabeled as ready capacity.
Confirmed hysteresis/cooldown, checkpoint rescale, shuffle preservation, and node autoscaling are not overstated as universal guarantees.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: Strong claims name bounds, lifecycle state, workload class, ownership assumptions, and controller scope.

evidence: Reviewed allocation-state timestamps, backlog/runnable age, useful parallelism, startup/restore/drain, churn, moved/recomputed work, and outcome metrics.
Confirmed no universal min/max, backlog/idle timeout, ramp factor, cooldown, stabilization, utilization, or allocation target is prescribed.
Confirmed the executable controller disclaims in-flight grants, service, locality, ownership, fairness, failure, and node supply.
Confirmed production decisions require matched baselines, correlated trace replay, canaries, multi-tenant victims, failure/transition injection, and rollback evidence.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: Cost is normalized to useful output and reviewed alongside completion/freshness, recovery, correctness, and fairness.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed allocation boundaries, elasticity classes, lifecycle states, static choice, actionable demand, bounded scale-up/down, shuffle/cache/state preservation, decommission, epochs, failures, fairness, node supply, cold starts, recovery, controller interaction, observability, and validation.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed implementable Spark/Flink/Hadoop-style controls, resource state machines, backlog and idle evidence, shuffle alternatives, checkpoint rescale, epoch reconciliation, quota, node-controller handoff, recovery minimums, canary metrics, and rollback. Internal practitioner-oriented review only.

pedagogical_review.notes: Verified progression from static/elastic contracts through controller signals and safe transitions to operations. Ten examples and five answered exercises cover phase allocation, work estimates, bottlenecks, shuffle, readiness, stateful rescale, epochs, recovery, coupled controllers, executable hysteresis, and production review.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external Spark/Flink/Hadoop/Kubernetes/Mesos/Borg/Omega maintainer, scheduler/control-systems researcher, data-platform/SRE/capacity/FinOps/security specialist, workload owner, accessibility specialist, or certification review is claimed.
